title: Premium Designer Grass for Homes, Balconies & Landscapes in India
metatitle: Designer Grass & Artificial Grass | Goals Floors
shortDescription: Designer Grass by Goals Floors is a versatile artificial grass option for balconies, terraces, rooftops, gardens and landscaped outdoor areas. Designed for residential and commercial use, it offers the look of outdoor grass with the practical benefits of artificial turf and easier day-to-day upkeep.
longDescription:
Designer Grass is artificial grass designed to create a natural-looking green surface in residential, commercial and decorative outdoor spaces. It can be used as artificial grass for balconies, terrace grass, rooftop landscaping, garden areas, cafés, resorts, office landscapes and other spaces where a consistent green finish is preferred over natural lawn maintenance.

For homeowners, one of the main advantages is flexibility. Artificial designer grass can be installed on suitable concrete, tiled or other prepared surfaces, provided the base is stable, reasonably level and able to handle drainage. It is also useful where maintaining natural grass is difficult because of limited soil, irregular sunlight or the practical demands of an urban balcony or terrace.

The appearance of artificial grass depends heavily on the construction, colour variation, pile arrangement and installation quality. A realistic product should look natural from normal viewing distances rather than appearing like a flat green carpet. A sample is worth checking in daylight because artificial grass can look slightly different under showroom lighting.

Is Designer Grass suitable for Indian weather? It can be suitable for Indian outdoor conditions when the product is selected appropriately for the application and installed correctly. UV resistance, drainage and surface preparation are important considerations, particularly for exposed terraces, rooftops and gardens. Artificial grass can also become warm under direct summer sunlight, so shaded areas and high-temperature locations should be considered during product selection.

Installation starts with measuring the area and preparing the surface. Cleaning, levelling, drainage, accurate cutting, positioning, joining and securing the edges all affect the final appearance. One thing people sometimes realise a little late is that the base matters just as much as the grass. If the surface is uneven, the finished installation can show those imperfections.

Maintenance is relatively straightforward but not completely maintenance-free. Leaves, dust and debris should be removed regularly, the grass can be brushed when needed, and occasional washing helps keep the surface fresh. Drainage points and edges should also be checked periodically, especially after periods of heavy rain.

Goals Floors primarily serves the Gurgaon and Delhi NCR market while assisting customers with artificial grass and flooring requirements across India. Customers comparing designer grass suppliers in India can discuss product selection, quantities, application requirements and installation considerations with the Goals Floors team before ordering.

installation:
1. Surface preparation: Inspect the installation area and determine whether the existing surface is suitable for artificial grass. Requirements can differ between concrete, tiles, soil and other bases.

2. Cleaning: Remove dust, loose material, weeds, dirt, grease and other debris so the grass can sit properly on the prepared surface.

3. Levelling: Correct significant uneven areas before installation. A good base is important because imperfections can remain visible through the artificial grass.

4. Drainage: Check that rainwater and cleaning water have a suitable route away from the installation. This is especially important on balconies, terraces, rooftops and outdoor landscapes.

5. Measuring: Measure the area carefully and allow for the layout, joins and cutting requirements. For larger areas, calculate the required quantity before ordering rather than guessing roll requirements.

6. Cutting: Position the grass and cut it carefully from the appropriate side using suitable tools. Avoid unnecessary cuts because accurate planning helps reduce visible joins and material waste.

7. Positioning: Lay the pieces in the planned direction and ensure adjacent sections are aligned consistently before fixing anything permanently.

8. Joining: Where multiple pieces are required, align the edges carefully and use an appropriate joining system or adhesive suitable for the installation surface and grass construction.

9. Securing edges: Secure perimeter edges and other required points so the grass does not shift during normal use. The fixing method depends on the underlying surface and installation conditions.

10. Brushing and finishing: Brush the grass to lift the fibres and distribute them naturally. Check the joins and edges and correct any visible alignment issues.

11. Final inspection: Inspect the complete area for uneven sections, visible joins, loose edges, drainage issues and finishing problems before the installation is considered complete.

Installation requirements vary according to the surface and location. Heavy rain is not the time to start an outdoor installation because surface preparation can become unnecessarily difficult.

installationSteps.title: Surface Inspection & Base Preparation
points: Inspect the installation area to verify the base is stable, clean, and crack-free.
Remove existing dust, loose debris, weeds, and oil residues for optimal adhesion.
Level any uneven dips or ridges to ensure the turf sits completely flat.

installationSteps.title: Drainage Verification & Slope Check
points: Verify adequate slope (minimum 1-2%) towards the drainage outlet.
Ensure rainwater runoff is unimpeded to prevent moisture pooling underneath.

installationSteps.title: Measuring, Roll Layout & Acclimation
points: Unroll the designer grass rolls with all pile fibers facing the same viewing direction.
Allow the turf to relax and acclimate under natural daylight for 1-2 hours to remove creases.
Carefully measure and dry-fit sections before making final perimeter cuts.

installationSteps.title: Precision Cutting & Seam Joining
points: Cut the backing cleanly using a sharp utility knife along the stitch gauge lines.
Align adjacent seams tightly and join them using high-strength seam joining tape and turf adhesive.
Firmly secure outer edges and perimeter borders to prevent shifting.

installationSteps.title: Final Power Brushing & Inspection
points: Brush the grass fibers against the grain using a stiff broom to lift the pile evenly.
Inspect all seams, edges, and drainage clearances for a seamless aesthetic finish.

maintenance:
Designer Grass is easier to maintain than a natural lawn, but it is not completely maintenance-free. Remove leaves, dust, soil and other loose debris regularly using a soft brush, blower or suitable manual method. Brushing the grass periodically helps keep the fibres upright and maintains an even appearance, particularly in areas with regular foot traffic.

Occasional washing can help remove accumulated dust and ordinary outdoor dirt. For spills or stains, clean them promptly using an appropriate mild cleaning method rather than allowing the material to sit for a long period. Avoid harsh chemicals unless they are confirmed to be suitable for the specific grass construction.

Drainage should be inspected periodically, especially after heavy rain. Make sure outlets and drainage paths are not blocked by leaves or debris. High-use areas may need more frequent brushing and cleaning than decorative areas.

Avoid dragging heavy sharp objects across the grass and take care with furniture, tools and other items that could damage or permanently flatten the fibres. Check perimeter edges and joins occasionally to make sure they remain secure. Good installation followed by simple, regular upkeep will help the grass maintain its appearance over time.

faqs.question: What is Designer Grass and how is it different from natural grass?
faqs.answer: Designer Grass is a type of artificial grass designed to provide a consistent green, grass-like appearance without the routine watering, mowing and soil maintenance associated with a natural lawn. The visual result depends on factors such as fibre construction, colour variation, pile arrangement and installation quality. It can be used for balconies, terraces, rooftops, gardens, landscaping and commercial decorative areas. Unlike natural grass, it does not grow or require mowing, but it still benefits from regular brushing, debris removal, occasional cleaning and drainage checks.

faqs.question: Is Designer Grass suitable for balconies and terraces?
faqs.answer: Yes, artificial Designer Grass can be suitable for balconies and terraces when the surface is stable, properly prepared and has adequate drainage. It is particularly useful in urban homes where there may not be enough soil or space for a natural lawn. Before installation, check the condition of the floor, water drainage and the amount of direct sunlight the area receives. A sample should ideally be viewed in daylight before ordering because colour and texture can appear different under showroom lighting.

faqs.question: Can artificial grass be installed on concrete?
faqs.answer: Artificial grass can generally be installed over a suitable concrete surface if the concrete is stable, reasonably level, clean and capable of draining water appropriately. Cracks, major uneven areas, loose material and drainage problems should be addressed before installation. The fixing and joining method depends on the specific surface and installation design. For balconies, terraces and rooftops, drainage is especially important because trapped water can create problems beneath the grass. The installation requirements should therefore be assessed according to the actual condition of the concrete rather than assuming every concrete surface is ready to receive grass.

faqs.question: Is Designer Grass suitable for Indian weather conditions?
faqs.answer: Artificial grass can be used in Indian outdoor conditions, but the product should be selected according to the location and exposure. For areas receiving strong sunlight, UV-resistant construction is an important consideration. Drainage is equally important during monsoon conditions, particularly on terraces, rooftops and landscaped areas. Artificial grass can become warm when exposed to direct summer sunlight, so this should be considered when choosing a product for frequently occupied areas. Proper surface preparation and installation are also important for maintaining the appearance and performance of the grass.

faqs.question: Does artificial grass get hot in direct sunlight?
faqs.answer: Yes. Like many outdoor surfaces, artificial grass can become warm when exposed to strong direct sunlight, especially during hot weather. The actual surface temperature depends on sunlight, surrounding conditions, ventilation, shade and the particular product. If the grass is being installed in an area where people frequently sit or walk barefoot, consider the amount of direct afternoon sunlight and whether shade is available. For balconies, terraces and rooftops in hot Indian climates, these practical conditions are worth discussing before selecting the product.

faqs.question: How should I clean and maintain Designer Grass?
faqs.answer: Routine maintenance is straightforward. Remove leaves, dust and loose debris regularly, and brush the grass when fibres become flattened by foot traffic or furniture. Occasional washing can help remove accumulated outdoor dust. Clean spills promptly using a suitable mild cleaning method and avoid chemicals that may damage the fibres or backing. Drainage points should be checked periodically so they remain clear, particularly during or after the monsoon. It is also sensible to inspect perimeter edges and joins occasionally. Artificial grass requires less routine work than natural lawn, but it should not be treated as completely maintenance-free.

faqs.question: How long does artificial grass last?
faqs.answer: The usable life of artificial grass depends on the product construction, UV exposure, installation quality, traffic level, maintenance and local weather conditions. There is no single lifespan that applies to every artificial grass product. Grass installed in a lightly used decorative balcony may experience very different conditions from grass installed in a busy commercial outdoor area. When comparing products, consider the construction, intended application, warranty information where provided and expected traffic. Proper installation and regular maintenance can also help the grass retain its appearance for longer.

faqs.question: Can Designer Grass be installed over an existing lawn or floor?
faqs.answer: It depends on what the existing surface is and its condition. A hard floor such as suitable concrete can often be prepared for artificial grass by cleaning, levelling where necessary and ensuring proper drainage. An existing natural lawn usually requires more preparation because vegetation, soil, moisture and unevenness need to be addressed before creating a stable base. Installing directly over an unsuitable or poorly prepared surface can result in an uneven appearance and drainage problems. The correct preparation method should therefore be chosen based on the existing site rather than using one installation method for every location.

faqs.question: How much artificial grass should I order for my area?
faqs.answer: Start by measuring the length and width of the installation area and calculating the approximate surface area. Then consider the roll dimensions, layout direction, joins and cutting waste. Irregular balconies, curved garden sections and areas with multiple corners may require additional material compared with a simple rectangular space. For larger installations, it is better to calculate the quantity before ordering rather than guessing the number of rolls. Goals Floors can assist with product selection and quantity planning based on the measurements and intended application.
